newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ABARE sees higher Australia aluminium production.
newsitem.headline: ABARE sees higher Australia aluminium production.

text.p: Australia's production of aluminium is expected to rise 11.7 percent to 1.56 million tonnes in 1997/98 (July/June) from an estimated 1.40 million in 1996/97, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said in its June commodities bulletin.
"The bulk of the production increase is expected to come from the Boyne Island expansion which is scheduled to reach full capacity by the September quarter 1997," ABARE said.
The existing Boyne Island smelter at Gladstone, Queensland, is 50 percent owned by Comalco Ltd, which will hold a 59.25 percent stake in the third potline.

ABARE, the Australian government's main commodities forecaster, said it expected continued strong demand on world markets for alumina for the remainder of 1997, and forecast Australian alumina output to increase by 3.1 percent to 13.57 million tonnes 1997/98 from 13.16 million in 1996/97.

The bulletin said the forecast alumina production increase was partly due to a 150,000 tonne capacity expansion at the Reynolds Metals Co Worsley refinery in Western Australia due to come on line late this year.
Export earnings from aluminium are forecast to jump by 34.2 percent to a record A$2.8 billion in 1997/98 as a result of increasing export volumes and prices, ABARE said.

"World consumption of aluminium is expected to grow strongly over the remainder of 1997 and into 1998, based on assumptions of strong economic growth and industrial production in key aluminium markets," ABARE said.
